trials.notes: Used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() and documented token APIs: next_token(), get_token_type(), is_tag_closer(), get_tag(), get_current_depth(), and get_modifiable_text(). Correctly chose the structural processor, guarded create_fragment() returning null, accumulated only #text tokens, and relied on decoded get_modifiable_text(). Minor near-miss: it uses an outer next_token() loop with an inner bounded next_token() walk for repeated headings, while the docs prefer single-loop state for repeated regions; it is still safe for these heading boundaries because virtual/real closers are visited.

Same documented API pattern as trial-1, with an extra PHP class_exists() guard that is not an HTML API call. No undocumented method use and no _doing_it_wrong records. Correctly handles uppercase tag names, empty headings, decoded entities, and implied heading closes. Minor idiom deduction for the nested next_token() walk despite the one-cursor warning for repeated-region extraction.

Used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() with a single next_token() state machine, matching the docs' recommended repeated-region pattern. All HTML API calls are documented. It tracks heading depth, appends only ordinary #text tokens through decoded get_modifiable_text(), flushes on depth drop, and handles empty/unclosed headings naturally.

failure_analysis: No hidden/frozen case failed across the three trials: each execution.json reports 7/7 passing cases and no _doing_it_wrong or trigger_error records. The docs did well by clearly steering subjects to WP_HTML_Processor for structural work, body fragments via create_fragment(), token walking via next_token(), subtree bounds via get_current_depth() with >=, and decoded ordinary text via get_token_type() === '#text' plus get_modifiable_text(). The implied-heading-close case was also supported by the next_token() documentation explaining that the HTML Processor visits closers for implicitly closed elements. The main near-miss is conceptual rather than functional: two trials used nested next_token() loops for repeated extraction even though the docs warn that a single cursor can make nested walks skip boundaries. The examples contain both single-subtree bounded walks and a single-loop repeated-region state machine, but the safe boundary between those patterns could be sharper.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs warn against nested next_token() loops for repeated regions, but nearby examples also show bounded subtree walks. Subjects can blur when an inner walk is acceptable and when it risks skipping the next region boundary.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short 'repeated subtree extraction' note contrasting valid patterns: use next_tag() to find each opener followed by a bounded inner subtree walk, or use one next_token() loop with explicit state; avoid an outer next_token() loop whose inner scan consumes a boundary the outer loop still expects to handle.

doc_gaps.problem: The depth contract is documented thoroughly, but the examples focus on explicit nesting. The important behavior for malformed/common HTML is that implicitly closed elements also produce virtual closers that end a depth-bounded walk.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a generic example of an element implicitly closed by a later sibling, showing the virtual closer's lower depth and explaining that this is reliable for tree boundaries but not proof that source bytes were complete.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs explain decoded text and special-element exceptions, but the common 'text content' contract could be easier to apply if it explicitly stated that concatenating #text tokens preserves source whitespace and does not synthesize spaces around inline markup.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add one sentence to the subtree text recipe: ordinary text extraction concatenates decoded #text tokens exactly as parsed; it does not insert separator spaces for tags, and any whitespace normalization is a caller-level policy.
